summary.oneLiner: An industrial minerals company that has evolved from supplying minerals to engineering performance-driven mineral-based solutions and specialty chemicals for construction, coatings, polymers and agriculture.
summary.business: 20 Microns Limited mines, beneficiates and micronizes industrial minerals (talc, kaolin, calcite, dolomite, silica) and processes them into specialty minerals, functional additives, construction chemicals and agriculture (MinFert) products for customers in paints and coatings, plastics and polymers, specialty chemicals, rubber, construction and agriculture. The Company sells over 50 specialty products domestically and through an international business serving export markets, supported by subsidiaries and joint ventures in minerals processing and building materials.

currentContext.strengths: Decades of expertise in mining, beneficiation and micronization of industrial minerals|Broad, diversified portfolio of over 50 specialty products deeply integrated into customer formulation processes globally|Differentiated, innovation-led products (e.g. self-healing Cracksil, White Kaolin Cosmetic Grade for global personal care markets) enabling technology differentiation and import substitution|Deepening technical/R&D and application-development capabilities supporting a shift toward solutions-oriented, higher-value positioning|Ongoing IT and digital transformation improving process integration and data-driven decision making across the value chain
currentContext.strategies: Structural shift from an industrial-minerals foundation toward a more specialised, innovation-led portfolio focused on advanced materials and speciality applications|Accelerating growth of speciality and high-performance materials|Scaling up emerging verticals such as the fertilizer (MinFert) and construction chemicals divisions|Expanding global footprint with a sharper focus on value-added, speciality export products and customer-specific solutions|Strengthening operational efficiency through technology and process/IT-digital integration|Maintaining a disciplined focus on capital allocation|Deepening technical capabilities, customer engagement and a solutions-oriented approach to product development, moving the business from mineral supply toward application partnership|Continued investment in long-term capabilities via capacity expansions, backward integration initiatives, and a calibrated approach to entering new geographies|Vision to be the global Minerals & Specialty Chemical industry benchmark for value creation and corporate citizenship
currentContext.expansion: The Company's three-year strategic roadmap is anchored in six growth pillars backed by a Rs.100 crore capex investment plan to be deployed over 24 months: (1) Capacity Expansion - upgrading infra-tech across existing and planned manufacturing/R&D facilities and strengthening quarrying for captive consumption; (2) Product Innovation - launching new variants across 4 breakthrough platforms and developing nano-mineral, bio-surface modifier and EV-battery mineral applications; (3) Export Acceleration - customer qualification in the EU, US, Middle East and ASEAN, leveraging 2-Star Export House status, with cosmetic-grade kaolin and HYPERTHERM UT positioned as near-term export anchors; (4) Strategic Partnerships & Acquisitions - the Sievert 20 Microns JV targeting a production ramp to 22,500 MTPA by FY29, and the Malaysian subsidiary targeting quarrying capacity of 92,000 MTPA and processing capacity of 1,08,000 MTPA by FY30; (5) Digital Transformation - rollout of an AI-powered CRM (20MCRM), vendor bank validation, GST verification and advanced EHS reporting; and (6) Sustainability & ESG - 15% of the capex plan directed to energy optimisation, waste reduction and green manufacturing, targeting a 15% reduction in carbon emissions over 3 years and 5-8% energy cost savings. Separately, per the CEO's message, the Company is securing backward integration through strategic mining acquisitions including its entry into Malaysian resources, with further expansions underway, and operates two R&D and product-application centres in Vadodara that are being aligned with future-facing sectors such as renewable energy and semiconductors.
currentContext.mdna: India sustained strong economic momentum in FY26 (Economic Survey 2025-26 projecting real GDP growth of ~7.3-7.4%), driven by robust domestic demand, expanding services/industry activity and resilient investment trends, with manufacturing GVA outpacing the broader industrial sector|India's mining sector showed robust momentum in FY26, with the National Critical Mineral Mission and infrastructure-led demand seen as structurally positive for industrial mineral producers|Across end-use industries, three structural shifts are benefiting the Company's positioning: customers moving from volume to value (performance-enhanced, specification-driven inputs), from cost to optimisation (yield/formulation efficiency, supply reliability), and from compliance to competitiveness (sustainability, traceability); the Company's mineral-based solutions are increasingly positioned in higher-value applications rather than commoditised supply chains|India's paints and coatings industry is projected to grow at roughly 6.5% CAGR to 2030, supported by automotive, construction and infrastructure expansion, urbanisation and rising disposable income - a key demand driver for the Company's mineral inputs|While certain legacy segments experienced moderated demand, the Company maintained consistent margins and continued to strengthen its positioning in higher-value segments|The 20MCC Fertilizer Division continues to gain traction, supported by increasing awareness around soil health and sustainable agricultural practices|The Construction Chemicals Division delivered encouraging growth, benefiting from strong momentum in infrastructure and real estate development and an expanding application footprint|International business remained resilient despite geopolitical disruptions and logistical challenges, with continued deepening of presence across key export markets and a sharper focus on speciality products and customer-specific solutions|FY27 macro outlook is viewed as positive but adjustment-oriented, with global trade uncertainty and tariff pressures on exporters expected to ease as domestic demand and investment strengthen

risks.note: Rated High impact: fluctuations in mineral availability, mining regulations, energy costs and logistics expenses may impact production costs and margins; mitigated via diversified/planned sourcing, captive mining reserves, strategic inventory management and long-term supplier partnerships.

Rated Medium impact: a slowdown in paints, polymers, rubber, ceramics or construction sectors could affect volumes and profitability; mitigated via a diversified end-market portfolio, expansion into specialty applications and customer diversification.

Rated Medium impact: trade restrictions, freight disruptions, currency volatility and geopolitical developments may affect export competitiveness and supply chains; mitigated via a balanced domestic-export mix, market diversification and active treasury management.

Rated Medium impact: delays in capacity expansion, integration of overseas assets, or operational disruptions may impact growth objectives; mitigated via structured project governance and performance monitoring systems.

Rated High impact: increasing environmental regulations, ESG expectations and compliance requirements may affect operating costs and market access; mitigated via ISO/Responsible Care practices and regular environmental audits.

Rated Medium impact: increased digitalisation exposes the Company to cybersecurity threats, data breaches and operational disruptions; mitigated via strengthened IT governance, cybersecurity protocols and disaster recovery systems.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
